[[File:Scomp_link.png|thumb|right|250px|A computer terminal]]

A '''computer terminal''' was a device that was used to gain access to a [[Computer/Legends|computer's]] mainframe and communicate information. There were several different devices used that could interface with a computer terminal via a [[Dataport/Legends|wall socket]], such as [[Scomp link/Legends|scomp links]] and [[Code cylinder/Legends|rank cylinders]]. They were mainly known as the perfect interface for [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]], though some maintenance points were made at the level of [[MSE-6 series repair droid/Legends|MSE-6-series repair droids]]. At [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]] there was a specific terminal that hooked up to [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] via a cable and downloaded the information about the [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star plans]]. On the first [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], R2-D2 hacked into a computer terminal to stop [[Garbage Compactor 3263827]]. On [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City's]] mainframe computer told R2-D2 that the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon's'']] [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] had been deactivated.

Another part of a computer terminal was more usable by [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]]; it had a interface that displayed information and allowed input through the use of the user's fingers or through other means according to how the terminal was made. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] used such a terminal to disconnect a [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] from the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star I's]] [[Reactor/Legends|main reactor]], allowing the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] to escape.
